import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 851

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
- [Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
-/

namespace Erdos851

/--
`TwoPowAddSet r` is the set of integers of the form `2^k+n`, where `k ≥ 0` and `n` has at most `r`
prime divisors.
-/
def TwoPowAddSet (r : ℕ) := {(2 ^ k + n) | (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r)}

/-- The set of integers of the form `2^k+p`, where `k ≥ 0` and `p` is prime. -/
def twoPowAddPrimeSet : Set ℕ := {(2 ^ k + p) | (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)}

/--
The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet := by
  sorry

/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r d,
    (TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d := by
  sorry

end Erdos851

findings.description: The conclusion `∃ r d, (TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d` adds a natural-density existence requirement. For each ε, it requires some r for which the counting ratios converge to a limit d. The source asks only that their liminf be at least 1 − ε. A lower-density bound does not require convergence, and neither the original problem nor the cited solution asserts this additional existence of a limit.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved” (1985), p. 75, explicitly asks whether for every ε > 0 there is an r such that the LOWER density of integers of the form 2^k + θ_r is greater than 1 − ε (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf). The cited Overleaf paper, Theorem 1, explicitly states `liminf_{x→∞} #(A_r ∩ [1,x])/x ≥ 1 − ε`; its following remark gives the same conclusion for distinct prime factors (https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion by `∃ r : ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity`. Also say “lower density” in the theorem’s docstring. The existing ε restriction and `research solved` category can remain.

reformulations.difference: Lean permits n = 0, since `Nat.primeFactors 0 = ∅`, whereas the cited paper explicitly requires n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This does not change any density assertion. The extra representations contribute only powers of two. For r ≥ 1, every such power except 1 already has a positive-n representation: 2^(j+1) = 2^j + 2^j, with at most one distinct prime divisor in the second summand. Thus the two sets differ only at 1. For r = 0, the positive-n set consists of 2^k + 1, while Lean additionally permits 2^k; both have density zero because their counting functions are O(log N). The positive-r set equality and preservation of natural density under insertion of one point were proved in Lean; the full equivalence including r = 0 was not formalized.

https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e — current LaTeX source, especially Theorem 1, its following remark, and the concluding proof
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf — pp. 74–76, especially the original question on p. 75
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanov%27s_theorem — statement and history, accessed through the Romanoff’s theorem redirect
Local implementation: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Density.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/PrimeFin.lean; Mathlib/Data/Nat/Factors.lean; Mathlib/Data/Set/Card.lean; Mathlib/Order/LiminfLimsup.lean
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Distinct prime-factor counting matches Erdős’s explicit definition of ω(n) and the Overleaf paper’s remark; the Romanoff variant is faithful. The restriction 0 < ε < 1 is harmless: the remaining ε ≥ 1 cases follow from the ε = 1/2 instance; this equivalence was proved in Lean. Both solved tags agree with the sources, including the current database’s affirmative status dated 2026-02-07. Live erdosproblems.com pages and discussion were Cloudflare-blocked, so the archived page was supplemented by the original paper, current Overleaf source, and current status database. Final checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, density.lean, and probe.lean compiled successfully. The reviewed file’s hash matches the committed version.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported defect is an additional natural-density limit-existence requirement, not a trivial contradiction or vacuity. I have no short proof or disproof of the exact statement for Erdos851.TwoPowAddSet. An unrelated set with lower density but no natural density would distinguish the notions generally, but would not refute this declaration.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created. The source comparison establishes the stronger-than-requested assertion, but does not establish that the formalized assertion is false.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported misformalization admits no short, honest proof or disproof that I can provide; settling the exact density-existence assertion would require additional nontrivial mathematics.

submission.summary: Replaced the natural-density existence requirement with `∃ r : ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity` and updated the docstring to say “lower density.” All other declarations and attributes were left unchanged. The edited file compiles with only the permitted `sorry` warnings.
